title: Growing Overnight Culture of OP50 as Worm Food
author: Priota Islam
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf5pjq5n
materials: Obtain sterile Erlenmeyer flask from the media kitchen

steps.title: Prepare LB broth
steps.instruction: Make at least 500 mL of LB broth using the following composition: 4 g NaCl, 4 g Tryptone, 2 g Yeast Extract, and add de‑ionised water to a final volume of 400 mL; then bring the total volume up to ≥500 mL for standardisation.

steps.title: Sterilise work area
steps.instruction: Wipe the bench with 70 % ethanol and create a relatively sterile environment by lighting a simple gas‑powered burner.

steps.title: Transfer LB to flask
steps.instruction: Add the desired volume of the prepared liquid LB broth to a sterile culture flask.

steps.title: Inoculate LB with colony
steps.instruction: Using a sterile inoculation loop, pick a single colony from an OP50 streaked LB agar plate (the plate can be stored at 4 °C for up to one month), dip the loop into the liquid LB broth, swirl to mix, and discard the loop.

substeps.instruction: Select a single colony from the streaked LB agar plate
Dip the loop into the liquid LB broth

steps.title: Cover culture loosely
steps.instruction: Loosely cover the flask with sterile aluminium foil or a non‑airtight cap to allow aeration.

steps.title: Incubate overnight with shaking
steps.instruction: Place the culture in a shaking incubator at the required growth temperature and incubate overnight.

steps.title: Check for growth
steps.instruction: After incubation, inspect the culture; successful growth is indicated by a cloudy haze in the media.

steps.title: Measure optical density
steps.instruction: Measure the culture’s optical density at 600 nm using a spectrophotometer, recording three readings, calculating the average, and using LB broth as the blank.
